article_title: Local Partnerships, National Impact: Year 1 of the Youth Mental Health Corps
citation: WestEd. (2025). Local Partnerships, National Impact: Year 1 of the Youth Mental Health Corps. https://www.wested.org/resource/building-a-model-of-student-centered-support-through-the-youth-mental-health-corps/
title: YMHC dual bottom line model: immediate student support plus long-term behavioral health workforce pipeline
description: The YMHC model pairs two purposes in one service program: young adult members (ages 18-24) provide relationship-centered near-peer mental health navigation to middle and high school students while simultaneously earning credentials and experience that build the behavioral health workforce. The report calls this "its dual focus on immediate student support and long-term workforce development," arguing the combination creates sustainability advantages because communities build local capacity while meeting immediate needs. Members recruit from the communities they serve to diversify the future workforce.
requirements: Members receive preservice training, site integration, ongoing supervision, career coaching, and credentialing opportunities
constraints: Near-peer supports do not replace clinicians or licensed providers; they facilitate referrals to professional care
target_learners: young adults ages 18-24 entering behavioral health careers
target_learning_goals: help-seeking and mental health support access
behavioral health career preparation and credentialing
examples: In Year 1 the YMHC deployed 317 members across 15 AmeriCorps programs and 172 service sites in Colorado, Michigan, Minnesota, and Texas

title: YMHC member training and support framework (preservice training, site integration, ongoing development, career coaching, credentialing)
description: The YMHC provides all members with a common support structure: intensive preservice training (which can include Youth Mental Health First Aid, trauma-informed care, mandated reporting, cultural competency, motivational interviewing, and suicide risk screening), site-based onboarding, weekly or regular supervision often from licensed professionals, individualized career coaching, and credentialing opportunities such as Community Health Worker or Certified Peer Support Specialist credentials. The report presents this framework as the core preparation enabling members to serve as near-peer navigators.
requirements: Partnerships with established nonprofits, schools, community organizations, and healthcare clinics to host and supervise members
constraints: Credential availability varies by location; the report states "In some locations, members can pursue additional credentials"
target_learners: young adults ages 18-24 serving as YMHC members
examples: Colorado members can enroll in the Colorado Community College System's Qualified Behavioral Health Worker I Certificate program; Michigan members earn five youth mental health certifications through Wayne State University's Community Health Worker Academy
